title: Unpacking Fear: Is Hell a Real Fear? #shorts

top_liked.author: @Dee.Murphy
top_liked.text: I was Paralyzing the petrified of hell. I’m jealous of people like you.

top_liked.author: @keturahspencer
top_liked.text: Realizing those relationships were already in that coffin and the final nail wouldn't significantly change anything was the hardest part. The next hardest thing was figuring out my identity afterwards, and stopping all prayer.

top_liked.author: @katwitanruna
top_liked.text: I’m so glad the two churches I went to as a child didn’t harp on hell. It was much more talking about God’s love. Personally I think Revelation is an apocalyptic fanfic.

top_liked.author: @ToniaEmily
top_liked.text: I had a much greater fear of God than a fear of Hell. During the worst times of the abuse I underwent as a child, the hardest thing to deal with is that I was taught to reach out to God when I was feeling afraid or hurt, but the fear and hurt I was undergoing was being inflicted…

top_liked.author: @rarebreed9208
top_liked.text:
I never feared punishment or hell, but got into Christianity because I thought it would be a community of decent, moral, like minded people who lived by precepts set forth by Jesus Christ.
  But boy, was I ever mistaken about both of them.

top_liked.author: @Coal1228
top_liked.text: I was lucky enough to grow up hearing about hell and thinking "That sucks, good thing I'm not going there" up until I started questioning my beliefs, at which point I had no reason to think there was a hell to go to.
